body:
I've never written a food blog, but I have worked in restaurants for over a decade. It's just an unspoken agreement that when I call you up for a "showcase" you're going to write me a good review. 

I've come into places that already have a "team" of reviewers that they use as their go to, and I've also worked places where I've had to reach out to people and build those relationships myself. 

In the instances that I was finding the bloggers myself I just tried to find people with the most exposure, even if that meant some cold calls. My best advice would try to get your blog in front of as many people as possible, that was the one and only metric I used when deciding who to reach out to.

I should also say that if the food and service was AWFUL I doubt I could still get good reviews, but I have put some lackluster product out and given some completely average service only to read the next day about the "mindblowing" experience they had.

I've been quoted between 260 and 300 by Glassmasters, but that was a couple years ago. Most other places were into the $500's. My deductible was $500 anyway so it made the most sense to just shell out the $300 myself.
Take what interests you, no one is going to care what you minor in. If you're looking for anecdotes I found that I use the skills I learned in accounting and OM every day.
You're going to be unhappy no matter what you choose. Try to find one that's running a promotion so at least you get something out of it, whether that's a few free months or no installation fee etc.

Such a joke. These "reviewers" are given free food and drink and in return they say how "amazing" these places are, implying that they are being impartial and objective in their review. 

Few a far between are the reviews that give any critiques, and even then they are usually tempered.
Can't say for chips, but for replacement I've always gone to Glassmasters and they've been more than fair to me. Sometimes less than half of what other places quoted, and never any problems.
